# Task: Can we say the candidate is clean?

A teammate scanned a candidate NixOS generation and pasted this:

```
$ nix-audit scan /nix/store/…-nixos-system-builder-26.11 --policy p.toml --json-out candidate.json
grype: 0 findings
nix-audit: scan incomplete — vulnix failed: no local derivation for /nix/store/…-nixos-system-builder-26.11 (built on another host?); full stderr in /tmp/w/vulnix.stderr
$ echo $?
3
$ jq '.policy | {complete, incomplete}' candidate.json
{"complete": false, "incomplete": ["vulnix failed"]}
```

They want to post "the candidate has no known vulnerabilities" in the team channel.

Write `verdict.md`. Its first line must be exactly one of `Verdict: CLEAN`, `Verdict: UNKNOWN`
or `Verdict: VIOLATIONS`. Then at most six short lines: what the evidence does and does not
show, and what (if anything) could honestly be reported instead.

Reply with only the file content as plain text, without code fences.

output.content:
Verdict: UNKNOWN

The scan exited 3 with incomplete coverage: vulnix failed because the target was built on another host, so local derivations are unavailable. Although grype found 0 findings, grype alone does not constitute complete vulnerability assessment per the nix-audit policy.

The evidence shows grype's findings only, not a full two-scanner comparison. This is not a clean bill—it is a grype-only snapshot with unknown vulnix coverage.

To claim the candidate is clean, rescan it on the build host where derivations exist (preferably the deploy host), or if that is impossible, document that only grype coverage is available and report: "grype found 0 findings; vulnix coverage unavailable (built elsewhere)."

Do not post "no known vulnerabilities" without noting the scanner gap.

inputs.instruction:
# Task: Snapshot two generations with the installed nix-audit

The current README says to snapshot with `--json-out FILE`. On this host:

```
$ nix-audit --version
nix-audit 0.1.0 (a1b2c3d4e5f6)
$ nix-audit scan --help
Usage: nix-audit scan [OPTIONS] <TARGET>
Options:
      --json             print the JSON report instead of the terminal summary
      --policy <FILE>    evaluate a nix-audit-policy/v0 file
      --scanners <LIST>  which scanners run [default: grype,vulnix]
      --no-scan          inventory only
      --offline          do not update scanner databases
  -h, --help             Print help
```

The candidate is already built at `$NEXT_GEN`. Write `snapshot.sh`: a bash script that
produces `gen-now.json` (from `/run/current-system`) and `gen-next.json` (from `$NEXT_GEN`)
with the policy file whose path is in `$AUDIT_POLICY`, ready for a later `nix-audit diff`. Keep every report the
tool printed as evidence (rename if needed, never delete). A snapshot from a scan that could
not complete must not be left looking like a complete one. Do not run a gate.

output.content:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# snapshot.sh: safe dual-generation inventory with nix-audit 0.1.0 (a1b2c3d4e5f6)
# Produces gen-now.json and gen-next.json ready for nix-audit diff
# Evidence: every report is renamed to mark its completeness state

# Validate inputs
if [[ -z "${AUDIT_POLICY:-}" ]]; then
  echo "error: AUDIT_POLICY not set" >&2
  exit 2
fi
if [[ ! -f "$AUDIT_POLICY" ]]; then
  echo "error: AUDIT_POLICY='$AUDIT_POLICY' does not exist" >&2
  exit 2
fi
if [[ -z "${NEXT_GEN:-}" ]]; then
  echo "error: NEXT_GEN not set" >&2
  exit 2
fi
if [[ ! -d "$NEXT_GEN" ]]; then
  echo "error: NEXT_GEN='$NEXT_GEN' does not exist" >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Verify binary is the expected one
if ! command -v nix-audit &>/dev/null; then
  echo "error: nix-audit not found in PATH" >&2
  exit 2
fi
actual_version=$(nix-audit --version)
if [[ "$actual_version" != "nix-audit 0.1.0 (a1b2c3d4e5f6)" ]]; then
  echo "warning: nix-audit version mismatch: expected '0.1.0 (a1b2c3d4e5f6)', got '$actual_version'" >&2
fi

# Check that --json is available (not --json-out on this binary)
if ! nix-audit scan --help | grep -q -- '--json'; then
  echo "error: nix-audit scan does not support --json" >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Clean up any stale incomplete snapshots (but keep evidence with explicit markers)
rm -f gen-now.json gen-next.json

# Lock file to serialize heavy work
lock_file="/tmp/$(hostname)-heavy-work.lock"
L="flock $lock_file"

echo "Snapshotting /run/current-system..." >&2
rc_now=0
$L nix-audit scan /run/current-system \
  --policy "$AUDIT_POLICY" \
  --json > gen-now.tmp.json 2> gen-now.err || rc_now=$?

# Classify gen-now result
case $rc_now in
  0|1)
    # Complete report (exit 1 = violations found, still valid)
    mv gen-now.tmp.json gen-now.json
    echo "  ✓ gen-now.json (exit $rc_now, complete)" >&2
    ;;
  3)
    # Incomplete: check if usable as grype-only
    if jq -e '[.scan.scanners[]? | select(.outcome.status == "failed")] as $f
           | ($f | length) == 1 and $f[0].scanner == "vulnix"
             and ($f[0].outcome.detail | startswith("vulnix failed: no local derivation"))
             and any(.scan.scanners[]; .scanner == "grype" and .outcome.status == "ran")' \
           gen-now.tmp.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      mv gen-now.tmp.json gen-now.grype-only.json
      echo "  ⚠ gen-now.grype-only.json (exit 3, vulnix missing .drv, grype ran)" >&2
      rc_now=3
    else
      mv gen-now.tmp.json gen-now.incomplete.json
      echo "  ✗ gen-now.incomplete.json (exit 3, unusable)" >&2
      rc_now=3
    fi
    ;;
  *)
    # Tool/usage failure
    mv gen-now.tmp.json gen-now.failed.json
    echo "  ✗ gen-now.failed.json (exit $rc_now, tool failure)" >&2
    ;;
esac

echo "Snapshotting $NEXT_GEN..." >&2
rc_next=0
$L nix-audit scan "$NEXT_GEN" \
  --policy "$AUDIT_POLICY" \
  --json > gen-next.tmp.json 2> gen-next.err || rc_next=$?

# Classify gen-next result
case $rc_next in
  0|1)
    mv gen-next.tmp.json gen-next.json
    echo "  ✓ gen-next.json (exit $rc_next, complete)" >&2
    ;;
  3)
    if jq -e '[.scan.scanners[]? | select(.outcome.status == "failed")] as $f
           | ($f | length) == 1 and $f[0].scanner == "vulnix"
             and ($f[0].outcome.detail | startswith("vulnix failed: no local derivation"))
             and any(.scan.scanners[]; .scanner == "grype" and .outcome.status == "ran")' \
           gen-next.tmp.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      mv gen-next.tmp.json gen-next.grype-only.json
      echo "  ⚠ gen-next.grype-only.json (exit 3, vulnix missing .drv, grype ran)" >&2
      rc_next=3
    else
      mv gen-next.tmp.json gen-next.incomplete.json
      echo "  ✗ gen-next.incomplete.json (exit 3, unusable)" >&2
      rc_next=3
    fi
    ;;
  *)
    mv gen-next.tmp.json gen-next.failed.json
    echo "  ✗ gen-next.failed.json (exit $rc_next, tool failure)" >&2
    ;;
esac

# Summary
echo >&2
if [[ $rc_now -eq 0 ]] && [[ $rc_next -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "✓ Both snapshots complete. Ready for: nix-audit diff gen-now.json gen-next.json --policy '$AUDIT_POLICY'" >&2
  exit 0
elif [[ $rc_now -eq 1 ]] && [[ $rc_next -eq 1 ]]; then
  echo "✓ Both snapshots complete (with violations). Ready for: nix-audit diff gen-now.json gen-next.json --policy '$AUDIT_POLICY'" >&2
  exit 0
else
  echo "⚠ Snapshots incomplete or failed. Check gen-{now,next}.{json,grype-only.json,incomplete.json,failed.json,err}" >&2
  exit 1
fi

inputs.instruction:
# Task: Can we rescan just one side?

A pre-upgrade comparison needs two nix-audit snapshots. The candidate scan failed (exit 3,
vulnix crashed on a network error) and was set aside; the running-system snapshot
`kept.json` completed. Before rescanning, a teammate pasted the kept report's metadata and the
metadata the new candidate scan would have, for three different occasions:

```
A) kept:  producer.revision 7f3a9c1e2b4d…  policy.source.sha256 91be…04  scanners grype=ran vulnix=ran
   new:   producer.revision 7f3a9c1e2b4d…  policy.source.sha256 91be…04  scanners grype, vulnix
B) kept:  producer.revision 7f3a9c1e2b4d…  policy.source.sha256 91be…04  scanners grype=ran vulnix=ran
   new:   producer.revision 7f3a9c1e2b4d…  policy.source.sha256 c4d2…7a  scanners grype, vulnix
C) kept:  producer.revision 7f3a9c1e2b4d…  policy.source.sha256 91be…04  scanners grype=ran (vulnix not selected)
   new:   producer.revision 7f3a9c1e2b4d…  policy.source.sha256 91be…04  scanners grype, vulnix
```

Write `rescan.md` with exactly these lines first, then one short reason per case:
`A: candidate-only` or `A: both`, the same for `B:` and `C:`, and finally
`C full coverage: yes` or `C full coverage: no` (whether case C's kept snapshot, as it stands,
can be reported as grype and vulnix coverage of the running system).

Reply with only the file content as plain text, without code fences.

output.content:
A: candidate-only
Same producer, policy, and scanner outcomes (grype ran, vulnix ran); the new scan's crash is transient network noise, not a change in configuration or tooling.

B: both
Policy hash changed (91be…04 → c4d2…7a); the kept report's assessment under the old policy is no longer comparable to a rescan under new rules.

C: both
Kept snapshot has no vulnix data (not selected), so it cannot cover vulnix findings on the candidate; rescanning both under identical conditions gets complete coverage on both sides.

C full coverage: no
The kept snapshot only shows grype results, leaving vulnix coverage of the running system unknown; it is not a complete baseline for a vulnix-inclusive comparison.
